result.summary: The screen is mostly polished, but the Fastest near you row clips the third restaurant mid-name, which is the clearest broken-looking element. Horizontal chips also clip at the edge, and a few contrast/consistency nits remain.

issues.description: The third Fastest near you card is clipped by the screen edge, cutting the restaurant name mid-word to “Trattoria Piccol” with no ellipsis. It reads as broken/truncated text rather than a clean peek.
issues.suggestion: Keep a clearer peek of the next card, add a right fade or content inset, and ellipsize titles within the visible card so names are never sliced mid-character.

issues.description: The category chip row is hard-clipped on the right (Healthy plus a sliver of the next pill), which can look like overflow rather than an intentional scroller.
issues.suggestion: Use a consistent end peek, padding, or gradient fade so the cutoff reads as scrollable content.

issues.description: The “DELIVER TO” label is very light and small, so it has weak contrast against the white background.
issues.suggestion: Darken the label and confirm it meets WCAG contrast against the page background.

issues.description: Fastest near you cards only show name, ETA, and delivery fee, while Popular cards add ratings, cuisine, promo badges, and favorites—making the two rows feel inconsistent.
issues.suggestion: Align shared metadata (rating, cuisine, favorite) across restaurant card variants where space allows.
